text:
The scoreboard said NYI by three, but the chances said something closer to a coin flip. Chicago deserved to win 53 percent of the time by the numbers, outshooting the Islanders in attempts 54 to 37 and generating 2.45 expected goals to New York's 2.91. At even strength the two sides were nearly level (1.76 to 1.69). What separated them was finishing and goaltending.

Bo Horvat supplied the finishing, with two goals. His power-play snap shot with 59 seconds left in the first period, a 2 percent chance, put New York ahead, and it was the only power-play goal of the night. Emil Heineman and Anthony Duclair then scored 2:54 apart in the second to make it 3-0. Ilya Sorokin turned aside 22 of 23 shots, saving 1.45 goals more than expected, while Arvid Soderblom allowed three on 18 shots against 2.26 expected.

The third period was where New York actually controlled play, out-chancing Chicago 1.24 to 0.81. Frank Nazar cut it to 3-1 at 17:26 on a slap shot, with Patrick Kane and Sam Rinzel assisting. Horvat answered 61 seconds later with a 65 percent chance, the most routine goal of the game, to seal it. Logan Stanley assisted on both Duclair's and Horvat's second goal, and the Islanders' defense quietly held their own against a heavier volume of shots.
